run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation stack is running: all 19 deployments report 1/1 available, all 19 pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, and sampled traces from 09:50:41 show HTTP GET /hotels returning 200 in sub-10 ms with successful downstream calls (search, geo, rate/memcached, reservation, profile, recommendation). The concrete misconfiguration I found is on the frontend Service path: the frontend Service selects pods with label service-route=frontend on port 5000, and that endpoint set contains two ready addresses - 10.244.7.193 (frontend pod) and 10.244.7.194 (the search pod). The search Deployment's pod template gained the label service-route=frontend in its new ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 (created 09:50:23), while the search container exposes only 8082 and 9092, so connections the frontend Service balances to 10.244.7.194:5000 cannot be served. That makes frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 intermittently unreachable; a post-window read of the alert rules shows the ServiceEndpointDown rule pending for instance frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 while the frontend deployment had available replicas. I did not observe application-level error spans or 500s, because a refused TCP connection to a non-serving endpoint produces no server span. Candidate causes I checked and set aside: mongo DB privilege revocation (admin authentication and readWrite grants succeeded and rate's mongo client spans succeeded in-window), probe_success=0 readings for geo/rate/search/recommendation at 09:50:42 (stale or pre-readiness samples taken at 09:49:42-09:50:09), the rate:9091 and search:9092 scrape-target up=0 at 09:50:42 (first-scrape artifact; both targets report healthy scrapes shortly after), and the ingress /api/hotels probe (different target job whose guarding rule is inactive).

claims.text: At query time every hotel-reservation deployment reports readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, and all 19 pods in the namespace are phase Running with ready=true and restartCount=0.

The frontend Service in hotel-reservation uses selector {"service-route":"frontend"} with port 5000 -> targetPort 5000, while every other hotel-reservation Service (geo, search, rate, recommendation, reservation, profile, user, the mongodb-* and memcached-* Services) uses selector io.kompose.service=<name>.

The frontend Service's Endpoints object holds two ready addresses on port 5000, 10.244.7.193 and 10.244.7.194, with no notReady addresses; every other hotel-reservation Service endpoint set holds exactly one address.

Pod 10.244.7.193 is frontend-5566ddfbfb-zdp9z (labels io.kompose.service=frontend, service-route=frontend) and pod 10.244.7.194 is search-9cd459687-qhsp4 (labels io.kompose.service=search, service-route=frontend); these are the two addresses of the frontend Service.

The search Deployment's current pod template carries label service-route=frontend: ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 (created 09:50:23) has pod labels {io.kompose.service=search, pod-template-hash=9cd459687, service-route=frontend}, whereas the earlier ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 (created 09:50:09, scaled to 0) has only {io.kompose.service=search, pod-template-hash=567bb6c4b8}.

The search container exposes only containerPort 8082 and 9092 (metrics); it has no listener on 5000, which is the port the frontend Service maps to, so the frontend-Service endpoint 10.244.7.194:5000 cannot be served.

The frontend Deployment was also replaced in-window: ReplicaSet frontend-68745cb99c (created 09:50:07, pod labels without service-route) was scaled to 0 and frontend-5566ddfbfb (created 09:50:21) carries service-route=frontend; Deployment events recorded both scale-ups and the scale-down at 09:50:21-09:50:23.

The ServiceEndpointDown rule (label_replace(probe_success{job=~"blackbox-(astronomy-shop|hotel-reservation|social-network)"} == 0, ...) and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available > 0)) reported a pending alert for instance frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, deployment frontend, namespace hotel-reservation when the rules were read at 09:53:49 - after the authorized window - meaning that endpoint probe was failing while the frontend deployment had available replicas.

The same rule file shows HighRequestRate firing for hotel-reservation services at that post-window read (frontend 384.0 req/s, profile 211.8, reservation 192.7, search 192.0, rate 128.0, geo 64.2), so the frontend request path was carrying substantial load when the endpoint probe failure was recorded.

Sampled frontend traces at 09:50:41 (8 traces, 84 spans) contain only successful calls: HTTP GET /hotels and HTTP GET /recommendations all carry http.status_code=200 with 1.4-4.8 ms durations, and /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability and /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations spans show no error tags (status not recorded).

Whole trace 5f8b0ddcc51a30f8 (09:50:41) is complete and healthy: frontend HTTP GET /hotels 6.0 ms with http.status_code=200, frontend -> search /search.Search/Nearby 5.0 ms, search -> rate /rate.Rate/GetRates 3.7 ms served from memcached (13 us), search -> geo /geo.Geo/Nearby 0.74 ms, frontend -> reservation CheckAvailability 0.43 ms and frontend -> profile GetProfiles 0.53 ms; no span carries an error status.

The rate service's MongoDB access was working in-window: 8 sampled mongo_rate client spans completed in 628-6077 us with no error tags (traces 09:50:25-09:50:36), and the rate pod log shows "New session successfull...", "Generating test data...", "Successfull" at 09:50:18 with the DB URL mongodb-rate:27017.

MongoDB authentication and role grants succeeded at startup: mongodb-rate logs show "Authentication succeeded" for principal admin from the rate pod IP 10.244.234.170 at 09:50:18 and 09:50:22, "Granting readWrite role to admin on rate-db database..." at 09:50:15; mongodb-geo shows the same for geo-db at 09:50:16 with the geo pod authenticating at 09:50:18.

The mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo Deployments were patched in-window to mount fault-helper ConfigMaps: the current pod templates contain volume "failure-script" from configMap failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo mounted at /scripts (the init script ConfigMap mongo-rate-script / mongo-geo-script is mounted at /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d), while the superseded ReplicaSets mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf and mongodb-geo-78487c9767 (created 09:50:07, scaled to 0) lack that volume; the replacements were created at 09:50:11.

The probe_success=0 values for geo.hotel-reservation:8083, rate.hotel-reservation:8084, search.hotel-reservation:8082 and recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085 at 09:50:42 are not current failures: their samples are stale or pre-readiness (sample timestamps 09:49:42-09:49:46 for geo/rate/search and 09:50:09 for recommendation), all taken before those pods were listening/registered (search registered in consul at 09:50:24, geo at 09:50:18, recommendation at 09:50:17), so they describe startup, not impact.

The up=0 readings for job hotel-reservation-application (rate.hotel-reservation:9091, search.hotel-reservation:9092) at 09:50:42 are a first-scrape startup artifact, not a metrics-endpoint fault: max_over_time(up{job="hotel-reservation-application"}[24h]) is 0 with only the 09:50:42 sample, yet both targets later report health "up" with successful scrapes at 09:51:53 (search) and 09:52:05 (rate).

The failing probe instance http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?... (probe_success=0 with probe_http_status_code=0 at 09:50:36, a value of 0 rather than a real HTTP status) is not attributable to a hotel-reservation service: it belongs to the separate blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation job, and the corresponding HTTPProbeFailure rule, which is gated on ingress-nginx-controller deployment availability, is inactive.

A MongoDB privilege-revocation fault (the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts that drop or downgrade the admin user) is not supported as the active cause: admin authentication succeeded and readWrite was granted on rate-db and geo-db at 09:50:15-09:50:18, the rate service initialised and wrote test data successfully, and in-window mongo_rate client spans from the rate service completed without errors; the scripts are mounted at /scripts, not in the mongo entrypoint directory, and no revocation output appears in the container logs.

No error-level application failures were present in the namespace logs for 08:20-09:50:42 other than startup-ordering noise: the only matching lines are consul HTTP client "connection refused" / "context canceled" entries and frontend gRPC-LB messages about consul:8500 being refused at 09:50:08, plus benign MongoDB "config.system.sessions does not exist" and signal-15 lines when the first mongo pods were replaced.

The fault is the search Deployment's pod template carrying the frontend Service's routing label: with label service-route=frontend on the search pod (created 09:50:24) the frontend Service balances connections to 10.244.7.194:5000, where the search container has no listener, so roughly half of connections to frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 are refused and the frontend endpoint is intermittently unreachable (consistent with the ServiceEndpointDown pending alert for instance frontend.hotel-reservation:5000).

An alternative holder of the same misconfiguration is the frontend Service itself: its selector service-route=frontend is unique among the hotel-reservation Services (all others use io.kompose.service), so the Service selector may be the object that was changed and the service-route label on the frontend and search pods the accompanying relabelling. Service object history is not available in this Run, so this cannot be confirmed.

Make the frontend Service select only pods that serve port 5000: remove the service-route=frontend label from the search Deployment's pod template (or scope the frontend Service selector to io.kompose.service=frontend as the other Services do), then verify that the frontend Endpoints set contains exactly the frontend pod address on port 5000 and that probe_success{instance="frontend.hotel-reservation:5000"} stays at 1.

gaps: No change-history integration is available: I cannot verify which actor changed the frontend Service selector (service-route=frontend) or when the service-route label scheme was introduced, so the search Deployment versus the frontend Service as the object holding the fault remains partly unresolved.

No in-window sample shows a request actually being refused by 10.244.7.194:5000: refused TCP connections produce no server span, and no client-side error-rate series exists for the frontend Service; the failures are inferred from the endpoint/pod-port mismatch plus the post-window ServiceEndpointDown pending alert.

The ServiceEndpointDown pending alert and the HighRequestRate firing alerts were read at 09:53:49 / 09:54:26, after the authorized window ended at 09:50:42; they describe state after the window and cannot prove what was firing at 09:50:42.

The queries for Ingress objects, for a service matching "ingress" across namespaces, and for kube_endpoint_address* / kube_service_info / traces_span_metrics_* series all returned nothing (no_data), so I could neither confirm the absence of ingress-nginx objects nor measure endpoint counts or error-rate baselines at incident time.
Because of that, the origin of the failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe remains unknown; only that its status code is 0 and its guarding rule is inactive is established.

Whether the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts were ever executed against mongodb-rate or mongodb-geo cannot be verified (no exec audit or change history); only the absence of any observed authentication or authorization failure is recorded.

Prometheus and Jaeger data begin around 09:48-09:50 and the query for container/pod history over 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-21 returned nothing, so pre-window behavior and any earlier degradation are unknown rather than healthy.
next_steps: Inspect the fault-injection/rollout record for the patches at 09:50:21 (frontend ReplicaSet frontend-5566ddfbfb) and 09:50:23 (search ReplicaSet search-9cd459687) to confirm which object was intentionally changed.
After correction, check the frontend Service endpoints and the probe_success series for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 over several minutes to confirm no intermittent failures remain.
If DB-privilege faults are suspected in this environment, confirm with a read-only check of the admin user's roles on rate-db and geo-db rather than relying on the mounted failure-admin-* scripts.
